findings.title: Revealed wisdom as practical restraint
findings.claim: The focus joins wisdom revealed by the Lord to a prohibition against rival allegiance, then makes that allegiance's consequence a casting and expulsion. Wider passages pair revealed direction with refusal of association and repeat the cast-out end for other misdirected orientations.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the focus's revelation verb, wisdom noun, passive casting verb, blame participle, and expelled participle. The independent triggers are 17:73's pressure to divert the messenger, 6:106's pairing of following revelation with exclusive deity and turning away from associators, 29:45's restraining effect of prayer, 50:26's parallel prohibition followed by casting into punishment, and 17:18's Hell, blame, and expulsion after seeking the immediate. These contacts make the focus's no-rival command read as practical revealed restraint with a wider consequence pattern.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning's final movement becomes part of the same revealed guidance named as wisdom: restraint addresses rival allegiance, and the outcome is an imposed cast-out state rather than a detached consequence.
findings.containment: The ordinary readings remain intact: revelation is still revelation, wisdom is not literally a bridle, and the Form IV passive tulqa still means being cast. The L-Q-Y encounter branch describes undergoing the named punishment, not a replacement translation. The 17:18 blame term differs from the focus term; only their paired blame-and-expulsion result is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication anchors the focus occurrences to the cited branches, and the packet supplies exact target Arabic for each contextual relation. Hiddenness and the encounter reading remain bounded contextual resonances, and target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Wisdom as a limit on rival authority
findings.claim: The focus's wisdom can carry a restraining role over the assignment of divine status: 17:42-43 presents alleged plural gods as dependent on and unable to surpass the Lord whom the focus refuses to place beside another deity.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's al-hikma and its no-rival imperative. The wider triggers are 17:42's conditional claim that supposed deities would seek a path to the Lord of the Throne and 17:43's statement of divine transcendence. Their contact turns the focus's restraint branch toward the assignment of authority itself, making the prohibition a limit on rival divine rank as well as an item in the ethical instruction.
findings.reader_payoff: The no-rival command becomes legible as a boundary on who may be assigned ultimate authority.
findings.containment: This retains only the wider 17:42-43 relation. It does not reconstruct the 17:34-38 ethical sequence, claim that 17:44's cosmic praise is present, or turn revelation into a written code. The target passages are supplied without morphology.

epistemic.reason: The source is legacy_unbound, but exact Arabic at 17:42-43 supplies a concrete wider trigger; the reading is a contextual extension and makes no target morphology claim.

findings.title: A contextual authority resonance
findings.claim: The focus's prohibition on making another deity can also resonate with refusal of a rival locus of judgment: 42:10 assigns disputed matters' judgment to Allah.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the focus's making construction with a rival-deity complement and its wisdom noun. The independent trigger is 42:10's statement that judgment of disputed matters belongs to Allah. These meet through the status assigned to an added deity and the context's allocation of ultimate judgment, extending the focus from a worship warning to a bounded authority resonance.
findings.reader_payoff: The rival-deity prohibition can be seen to touch not only the object of devotion but also a competing claim over ultimate decisions.
findings.containment: This is a contextual extension, not a claim that all human jurisdiction is idolatry or that worship and authority are identical. Whether the authority resonance is coextensive with worship remains unresolved, and the target is supplied without morphology.

epistemic.reason: The HFT summary is legacy_unbound and has no anchor trace; the authority reading is independently bounded by the focus surface and exact 42:10 target text, without assigning target morphology.
